items.prompt:
Which sentence is a FACT that belongs in informative writing?
A) I think butterflies are pretty.
B) Butterflies grow from caterpillars in a process called metamorphosis.
C) I love going to the butterfly garden.
D) Butterflies are my favorite insect.

steps: Facts are true statements that can be checked. Options A, C, and D all express personal feelings or opinions.

items.prompt: Write two facts about dogs for an informative paragraph.
items.answer: Sample: Dogs are mammals that have been pets for thousands of years. They can be trained to follow commands and help people in many jobs.

steps: Facts are statements that are true and can be proven. Avoid 'I think' and personal feelings.

items.prompt: What is the job of an introduction sentence in an informative paragraph?
items.answer: The introduction sentence names the topic and tells the reader what the paragraph is going to be about.

steps: The introduction sentence comes first. It introduces (names) the topic so the reader knows what they will learn.

items.prompt: Write an introduction sentence for an informative paragraph about the moon.
items.answer: Sample: The moon is a large rocky body that orbits Earth and can be seen in the night sky.

steps: Start with 'The moon is...' and add a factual description.

items.prompt: Is this a fact or an opinion? 'Giraffes are the tallest animals on land.' Explain how you know.
items.answer: It is a fact because it can be measured and proven to be true.

steps: Facts can be checked or measured. This statement can be proven by measuring giraffes.

items.prompt: Write a concluding sentence for this informative paragraph about trees: 'Trees are large plants that have roots, a trunk, branches, and leaves. Trees provide oxygen, food, and shelter for many animals.'
items.answer: Sample: Trees are one of the most important living things on our planet.

steps: A concluding sentence wraps up the paragraph. It often restates the topic or explains why it matters.

items.prompt:
Which sentence does NOT belong in an informative paragraph about sharks?
A) Sharks are fish that live in the ocean.
B) Sharks have sharp teeth that they replace throughout their lives.
C) I think sharks are scary and dangerous.
D) Some sharks can grow up to 40 feet long.

steps: Informative writing sticks to facts. 'I think sharks are scary' is a personal opinion and does not belong.

items.prompt: Write an introduction sentence and one fact sentence for an informative paragraph about snow.
items.answer: Sample intro: Snow is a type of frozen precipitation that falls when temperatures drop below freezing. Fact: Each snowflake has a unique six-sided shape and forms around a tiny piece of dust in the clouds.

steps: Introduction: define or describe snow. Fact: add one true statement about snow.

items.prompt:
Put these sentences in the correct order for an informative paragraph:
A) The ocean is home to millions of sea creatures, from tiny fish to giant whales.
B) Oceans cover about 70 percent of Earth's surface.
C) The ocean is one of the most important parts of our planet.
items.answer: B, A, C (or C, B, A with C as the introduction)

steps: Introduction first (names the topic), facts in the middle, concluding statement at the end. B or C can serve as the introduction; the most natural order is B (fact about coverage), A (what lives there), C (concluding statement of importance).

items.prompt: Write two facts about apples to use in an informative paragraph.
items.answer: Sample: Apples are fruits that grow on trees in many parts of the world. They come in many colors, including red, green, and yellow.

steps: State two true things about apples without expressing a personal opinion.

items.prompt:
What is MISSING from this informative paragraph? 'Bears are large, furry mammals. They eat berries, fish, and honey.'
A) An introduction sentence
B) A fact
C) A concluding sentence
D) Nothing is missing

steps: The paragraph has an introduction and a fact but no concluding sentence to wrap it up.

items.prompt: Write a complete informative paragraph (3 sentences) about rain. Include an introduction, one fact, and a concluding sentence.
items.answer: Sample: Rain is water that falls from clouds in the sky. Rain forms when water vapor in the air cools and turns into tiny droplets that join together and fall to Earth. Rain is important because it fills rivers and lakes and helps plants grow.

steps: Sentence 1: introduction (what is rain). Sentence 2: fact about how rain forms. Sentence 3: concluding sentence about why rain matters.

items.prompt:
Choose the BEST introduction sentence for an informative paragraph about recycling:
A) Recycling is really fun!
B) I love to recycle at home.
C) Recycling is the process of turning used materials into new products.
D) Everyone should recycle.

steps: A good informative introduction states facts and introduces the topic clearly. Option C gives a factual definition. A and B express opinions; D is more of a command.

items.prompt: Write one fact and one definition for an informative paragraph about plants.
items.answer: Definition: A plant is a living thing that uses sunlight, water, and air to make its own food. Fact: Plants produce oxygen that animals and humans need to breathe.

steps: A definition explains what something is. A fact gives a true detail about it.

items.prompt:
Complete this informative paragraph by writing the missing introduction sentence and concluding sentence.

'___. Caterpillars hatch from eggs and spend their time eating leaves. Then each caterpillar forms a chrysalis and slowly transforms. When the chrysalis opens, a butterfly emerges with colorful wings. ___.'
items.answer: Introduction: The life cycle of a butterfly has four amazing stages. Concluding sentence: This incredible process of change is called metamorphosis.

steps: Introduction: introduce the topic (butterfly life cycle). Concluding sentence: wrap up by naming the process or stating its significance.
